messages:
Jordan: FYI customer wants an air-gapped POC but insists on an offline component catalog that can be shipped in chunks. They want a clear rollback plan and need cost delta for licensed Dedicated vs hosted. POC kickoff next Wed. @Meera can you confirm feasibility?
Meera: I can lead. quick Q: do they require per-component signing + SBOM or is image-level signing fine?
Jordan: They said "artifact provenance for each bundle" and legal called out SBOMs per bundle. Also strong preference for small incremental updates (delta) instead of full redeploys.
Meera: Ok — we can do chunked bundles with per-bundle SBOM + signature. Two implementation approaches:
- monolithic tarball that we ship and apply (simpler but large downloads)
- chunked catalog where we deliver deltas/patches and the agent composes (better bandwidth)
Sam: Technical constraints: the agent currently supports applying a single signed bundle atomically. To support chunked deltas we'd need a small bootstrap change (KV manifest + merge logic). Estimate ~3-4 dev days for a safe POC hack, 2 weeks for hardened release.
Meera: For rollback we can keep dual-manifest: previous manifest pinned locally so agent can revert to last-good. That adds ~1 dev day to the POC flow.
Maria: Security notes: signatures must use customer KMS integration (HSM optional). We'll need the signing public key to be listed in the bundle metadata and we must verify SBOM checksums before applying. Also we need to document our chain-of-trust for the SOC/ISO questionnaire.
Jordan: Good — that'll satisfy legal. Can someone sketch the minimal upgrade command we can give ops?
Sam: Example apply command for POC:```bash
redwood-agent apply-bundle --manifest /path/catalog.json --bundle-dir /mnt/offline/chunk-42 --verify-signature
```
Meera: For delta strategy the manifest would look like:```json
{"bundles": ["base-v1.tgz","patch-1.tgz","patch-2.tgz"], "signatures": {"base-v1.tgz": "sig..."}}
```
Jordan: Pricing question from buyer: what is the estimated uplift for offline packaging + signed bundles on Dedicated vs standard hosted?
Meera: Ballpark: for small POC (<=3 nodes) we recommend a one-time engineering packaging fee + a minor SKU uplift for air-gapped support. Rough numbers: $15k one-time + 10-15% monthly Dedicated premium. I'll confirm exacts with finance.
Jordan: Perfect. Any enterprise blockers we should raise now?
Maria: Key blockers: 1) customer requires FIPS-compliant signing (check their HSM type), 2) patch window restrictions — they may allow only monthly installs, that forces bigger delta sizes and more careful testing, 3) offline telemetry policy (we need opt-in local logs only).
Sam: Ops note: if their network is extremely constrained we'll need to chunk bundles <100MB each. That will increase number of artifacts and signing overhead. Also consider gzip-levels and rsync-friendly deltas.
Meera: Action items: 1) Jordan — confirm exact HSM/KMS vendor and allowed weekly/monthly windows with customer (by EOD Monday) 2) Sam — spike for bootstrap+rollback (3-4 days) and share patch CLI by Tues 3) Maria — draft SOC answers for per-bundle SBOM & signing (by Tues) 4) Meera — get pricing confirmation from finance (by Tue afternoon).
Jordan: I'll ping customer and update timeline. Thanks team :thumbsup:
DeployBot: Build artifact uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.example/poc/offline-catalog/v1/chunk-42.tgz (signed) :package:
Meera: Noted, will use that for the dev spike.
Jordan: Closing loop — will update the opportunity with these action items and the rough budget. If finance confirms uplift I'll add to the proposal.
Meera: Also: recommend we include a short-runner script for customers to validate signatures locally before apply, reduces ops risk. I'll prototype it in the spike.
Jordan: Great. Meeting scheduled Tue 10am with customer to finalize HSM details.
